To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the laboratory preference scale, the laboratory scale and demographic variables, and the laboratory scale and media variables, are the three best predictors of brand purchases in the tooth paste and cake mix product category, but that the laboratory scale and activity variables are the best predictor in the liquid household cleaner product category.

the laboratory measures of preference are a significant predictor of brand purchases in a product category, and that the predictive power of these measures is greater for the product categories studied than that of the other independent variables used in our model.
the models based on laboratory measures of preference have greater predictive power than models based only on survey measures of demographic and attitudinal characteristics of consumers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What are the relative contributions of preference and demographic variables in predicting consumer purchases of brands?
the development and testing of a set of models that predict the purchase of specific brand products.
the use of laboratory preference measures as predictors of consumer purchases in the market place.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a laboratory preference measure can be a useful addition to other consumer characteristics when attempting to explain brand purchase behavior.
the preference scale is a useful tool in predicting brand purchases.
the laboratory preference scales are not a perfect predictor of actual brand purchases in the marketplace.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an empirical model that is useful in the short run, and which is consistent with the theoretical model.
the models are not very powerful in predicting brand purchase, but they are useful for understanding the relationship of brand preference to the characteristics of individual consumers.
the laboratory brand preference scales are a useful tool for the prediction of actual purchases in the marketplace.
The main takeaway from our work is that
laboratory preference scales are useful predictors of consumer brand purchases.
the laboratory brand preference scales, when combined with the demographic, media exposure and attitudinal measures, are able to predict consumer purchases in the market.
the laboratory measures of brand preference can be used to predict brand purchases with a high degree of accuracy.
